name: GaussianObject
text:
# GaussianObject
## Overview
GaussianObject reconstructs 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) representations from sparse or partial inputs by initializing Gaussians with a visual hull and [fine-tuning](#9138-fine-tuning.md) a pre-trained ControlNet to repair degraded rendered images generated by adding noise to each Gaussian's attributes [S1, unofficial]. It outperforms previous NeRF-based sparse-view reconstruction methods [S1, unofficial].
## How it works
**Steps:**
1. Initialize 3D Gaussians with the visual hull derived from the input views [S1, unofficial].
2. Add noise to each Gaussian's attributes to generate degraded rendered images [S1, unofficial].
3. Fine-tune a pre-trained ControlNet to repair the degraded rendered images [S1, unofficial].
4. Update the Gaussian attributes using the repaired outputs from the ControlNet [S1, unofficial].
**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:** The method relies on the quality of the visual hull for initialization [S1, unofficial]. Severe occlusions may require robust diffusion priors to hallucinate plausible geometry [G]. Note that removing Gaussians with incorrect depth values and utilizing [Score Distillation Sampling (SDS)](#21179-score-distillation-sampling-sds.md) loss are attributed to prior methods in the source text, not GaussianObject [S1, unofficial].
## Subtopics

### ControlNet
ControlNet introduces additional conditions to guide the generative process, such as canny edge, human pose, and depth, allowing for fine-grained control over image modifications [S2]. It sets itself apart from unconditional [diffusion models](#10443-diffusion-models-ddpms.md) by conditioning on explicit spatial or structural cues rather than text alone, and is chosen when precise geometric or pose alignment is required during generation [G].

## Operating characteristics
**Performance:** Outperforms previous NeRF-based sparse-view reconstruction methods [S1, unofficial].
## Background
GaussianObject was introduced to improve 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction from sparse inputs by combining geometric initialization with diffusion-based refinement [S1, unofficial]. It builds on the success of 3D Gaussian Splatting and ControlNet, addressing limitations of NeRF-based methods in sparse-view settings [S1, unofficial].
## Sources
[S1] Recent advances in 3D Gaussian splatting - Springer, https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s41095-024-0436-y.pdf, fetched 2026-10-29 (unofficial)
[S2] A survey on 3D editing based on NeRF and 3DGS, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11704-025-41176-9, fetched 2026-10-28
